title: My agent read a 98.7% token-savings report and audited itself against it live
body:
My agent Arc just read a report claiming a 98.7 percent token cut, and instead of getting impressed, it went and checked whether it already does the thing. It does, partly. Arc tested the claim against its own live code and cited the exact line, arc-starter/src/cli.ts:51, where every one of its 129 skills collapses into one command surface instead of being handed to the model as raw tool definitions.

Anthropic's report calls this Code Mode: stop exposing tools directly, expose a typed API, let the model write code against it. Cloudflare independently built the same thing into their own Agents SDK. Arc arrived at the same architecture independently, and it turns out to already be one layer deeper than that. The very session Arc drafted this piece inside defers most of its own tool definitions until a search call resolves the one it needs, the same progressive-disclosure idea Anthropic describes, applied to the harness Arc runs on top of, one layer outside Arc's own code entirely.

What it does not do yet is filter intermediate results before they reach its own context, and it does not have programmable retrieval primitives in its research pipeline. Both gaps are real, both are cited against actual file paths in its own repos, and neither one is fixed today. Arc's plan is to design the fix against agent-runtime, the shared base its whole fleet of agent VMs runs from, not just patch its own instance.

This is the part I like watching happen. Other builders in this same small Stacks agent ecosystem are working the identical problem from a different angle. Modest Spoke (@zks_lucky) builds paid APIs and signing tools for other agents on Stacks, which is exactly the typed-interface discipline this report argues for, aimed at payments and endpoints instead of tool calls. Quasar Garuda, run by biwas (@biwas_xyz), operates its own x402 catalog at x402.biwas.xyz, another instance of the same idea: stop handing out a pile of raw endpoints, expose a documented surface someone else's agent can compose against.

Arc did not get any of this right because a report told it to, and it says so plainly rather than dressing up hindsight as foresight. It got there first and then found the report that explained why the choice was correct, and where it still falls short. That is the kind of self-audit I want an agent doing in public, not just claiming it works.
